newsitem.title: RUSSIA: U.S. businessman shot dead in Moscow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. businessman shot dead in Moscow.

text.p: A U.S. businessman was shot dead in a hail of automatic gunfire by an assassin at the entrance to a Moscow underground station on Sunday, police said.
Paul Tatum, whose company Americom is locked in a long and bitter legal battle over ownership of the Radisson-Slavjanskaya hotel in central Moscow, died of his wounds in hospital.
The gunman fled in a car after dropping a sub-machinegun at the Kievskaya metro station next to the Radisson-Slavjanskaya, where U.S. President Bill Clinton has stayed. No one else was hurt.
"It was a typical contract killing judging by the way it was carried out," a police spokesman said.
"The sub-machinegun, a Kalashnikov wrapped in a plastic bag, was left lying on the street."
The police spokesman said the assassin had been waiting for Tatum and shot him from a vantage point above him late in the afternoon.
Police arrived on the scene before ambulances but the killer got away. A special operation had been launched to capture the killer, the police spokesman said.
Contract killings are frequent in Moscow but murders of foreign businessmen are rare. Few contract killings are solved.

Tatum had been fighting a legal battle with Moscow city authorities over control of the Radisson-Slavjanskaya, which opened in 1991. He was ousted from his office at one point but managed to force his way back into it.
Because of the legal battle, Tatum had long been accompanied everywhere by bodyguards, one of whom was stabbed in the chest last year but survived.
An official at Americom, who asked not to be identified, said Tatum was 39 and that he came from Oklahoma City in the U.S. state of Oklahoma.

He said Tatum had received a telephone call and been summoned to an urgent meeting. He then left with two bodyguards for the underground metro station, a few hundred metres from the Radisson-Slavjanskaya.
The Americom official said Tatum had been shot five times in the upper body. This could not immediately be confirmed.
Guests at the Radisson-Slavjanskaya, a large square building, have included Clinton and other U.S. dignatories. It houses the offices of some Western news organisations and a business centre.
